physical_gate_negative_lane.meaning: Locking a replaceable lockfile pathname is insufficient physical singleton evidence because a live holder retains the old open-file-description lock while a contender can open and lock a newly materialized inode.

physical_gate_repair_lane.mechanism: flock an open state-directory FD and verify FD-to-path device/inode identity on acquire, heartbeat and release

initial_run_adjudication.cause: Immediate unlink/recreate on ext4 reused the just-freed marker inode number, so the test incorrectly assumed path replacement always implies a numerically different inode.

test_only_fix.change: Keep an unflocked descriptor to the pre-intervention marker open across unlink/recreate so inode-number recycling cannot alias the old and replacement directory entries; compare replacement path identity to the preserved old open-FD identity.

physical_gate_repair_lane.promotion_boundary: Even a future green marker-replacement regression proves only the measured marker-path repair; PR #235 independently proves the whole state-root pathname remains a higher-order singleton dependency.

external_primary_evidence.source: etcd documentation — etcd versus other key-value stores
external_primary_evidence.design_implication: Lease/lock state by itself is not sufficient protection for external resources; downstream effect boundaries need generation/version validation.

external_primary_evidence.source: Burrows, The Chubby lock service, OSDI 2006
external_primary_evidence.design_implication: A sequencer/generation validated by the receiving service prevents stale lock holders from acting as current.
flock locks are associated with open file descriptions; pathname replacement is not equivalent to replacing a live open-file-description lock.

rename leaves existing open file descriptors unaffected and requires permissions at the containing-directory boundary; parent-directory authority can therefore become an explicit deployment fence against state-root replacement.

A persistent service state directory can be created and managed under the system state namespace while remaining writable to the service, enabling the parent namespace to be controlled separately from in-state writes.

exactly_one_out_of_box_experiment.intervention: While holder A retains the repaired state-directory FD/flock, rename the entire disposable state-root pathname away, materialize a fresh migrated state root at the original path, let contender B enter the real repaired Gate, then force A through its next anchor path-identity heartbeat check.
exactly_one_out_of_box_experiment.hypothesis: Directory-FD locking closes lockfile-entry replacement but cannot by itself prevent a replacement state-root pathname from creating a second independent physical and semantic generation before the old holder reaches its next path-identity check.
exactly_one_out_of_box_experiment.strongest_counterhypothesis: Production ownership/mount/service policy makes state-root rename/replacement unreachable to Frank and all allowed tools; if measured true, an explicit deployment invariant can close this class without another runtime lock architecture.

hypothesis_matrix.claim: The whole state-root pathname remains a higher-order physical singleton dependency above the directory-FD repair.
hypothesis_matrix.evidence: Target run 31413758588 admitted two live real Gate leases at semantic epoch 1 on distinct state-directory inodes before the old holder's next heartbeat fenced itself.

hypothesis_matrix.claim: Runtime lock redesign beyond the directory-FD repair is unnecessary if accepted deployment makes the state-root entry non-replaceable by the Frank runtime while preserving legitimate in-state writes.
hypothesis_matrix.next_test: On the accepted target deployment, bind production state to an explicitly managed namespace (systemd StateDirectory or equivalent root-owned parent/mount policy), prove the Frank service identity cannot rename/delete/replace the state-root entry, and simultaneously prove normal state writes, migrations, restart, recovery and rollback procedures still work.

architecture_delta.physical_singleton_decision: Do not promote a replaceable-path flock or state-directory FD alone as the global CURRENT-instance singleton boundary. Prefer an explicit OS/deployment namespace boundary whose parent/mount authority is not writable by the Frank runtime, while the state contents remain writable. If accepted deployment cannot enforce that property, anchor physical singleton/incarnation identity outside the replaceable state root.
architecture_delta.candidate_deployment_mechanism: systemd StateDirectory-managed persistent state plus root/deployment-controlled containing namespace, optionally combined with existing service sandboxing, is a high-value simple candidate; exact path/name and unit policy remain unselected until repository/deployment truth is measured.
architecture_delta.restore_boundary: Deployment path immutability does not solve authorized snapshot/restore rollback. Existing #197/#207 negative evidence remains a separate conjunctive requirement for a non-rollback restore/incarnation generation before restored state becomes runnable.
architecture_delta.effect_on_pr225: Retain #225 as the narrow marker-file replacement repair candidate; even a green corrected run is insufficient for global singleton promotion without the outer namespace discriminator.
architecture_delta.effect_on_pr228: PR #228 can prove exact issuance by its Gate but cannot prove that Gate is the sole possible global current Gate until physical namespace and process/restore incarnation dependencies are closed.
architecture_delta.rollback: No product architecture was promoted by this run; PR #225 remains draft and PR #235 remains diagnostic-only.
